Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-boost-polish-medium-0027", "row_sha256": "6522baa48ead11f5416a962c10f9fe54c2e0c2ab51e3cbcd7eb99dda165a926e", "mode": "/polish", "language": "en", "context": {"profile": "Clear and professional."}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Rewrite awkward phrasing into readable prose for the supplied profile, or plain prose when none is supplied. Preserve intent and certainty. Do not add a greeting, subject, signature, conclusion, or fact that the input did not supply.", "input": "the board-game lending shelf is beside the reception desk at the Maple Street community room. it has 24 games, with the titles written on a clipboard next to it, and the shelf is available whenever the room is open, from 9 a.m. to 8 p.m. tuesday through saturday. people can borrow one game at a time, and the loan is for two weeks. to check one out, they write their name, phone number, and the date on the card in the box, then leave the card with the desk volunteer. when they bring a game back, they put it on the return table rather than straight onto the shelf, so someone can check that all the pieces are there. this part of the process is perhaps slightly awkward when the desk is busy, because the return table is close to the entrance and can get crowded. the volunteer usually checks returns before the end of the day, but the shelf does not list when a particular game will be put back out. missing pieces should be written on the card, although i think the instruction could be easier to notice. the shelf includes family games and a few longer strategy games, and the clipboard has a short note about the age range for each title.", "output": "The board-game lending shelf is beside the reception desk at the Maple Street community room. It holds 24 games, with the titles listed on a clipboard next to the shelf. The shelf is available whenever the room is open, from 9 a.m. to 8 p.m., Tuesday through Saturday.

People may borrow one game at a time for two weeks. To check out a game, they write their name, phone number, and the date on a card in the box, then leave the card with the desk volunteer. When they return a game, they place it on the return table rather than directly on the shelf so someone can check that all the pieces are there. This part of the process can be slightly awkward when the desk is busy, since the return table is near the entrance and can get crowded.

The volunteer usually checks returns before the end of the day, but the shelf does not indicate when a particular game will be put back out. Missing pieces should be noted on the card, although I think this instruction could be easier to notice. The shelf includes family games and a few longer strategy games. The clipboard has a short note about the age range for each title."}]
